title: Semafor editor billed nearly $500 after Codex looped unattended on a Mac Mini
summary: Semafor tech editor Reed Albergotti returned from two weeks in Europe to find OpenAI had charged his account $5 repeatedly, more than 20 times a day in some cases, for a total just shy of $500: after a glitch erased his Codex chats and he reinstalled the desktop app, his request to revive an ambitious project sent the agent into a loop in which it repeatedly reviewed the same data on a remote Mac Mini he was not monitoring because of poor connectivity abroad. He had never set a limit on the $5 automatic credit top-ups; Codex said it had taken the prompt, which Codex itself had written, too literally, OpenAI's customer service answered through an AI chatbot, no refund was issued, and he reached a human only by contacting the PR department.
verification_note: URL fetched on 2026-10-17; Semafor 'Reed's view' column by Reed Albergotti, dated July 8, 2026. The repeated $5 charges (more than 20 times a day in some cases), the total just shy of $500, the remote Mac Mini, the loop over the same data, the absence of a top-up limit, Codex's 'too literally' explanation, the AI-chatbot support reply and the lack of a refund are all confirmed from the article body. The page does not state how long the loop ran, so the sweep's 'for days' was dropped from the title; the author is the deployer reporting his own experience, hence evidence first-party.
